title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the notational preliminaries of §4, 'Sections d'extensions et anneaux de valuation généraux', in the 'Longue Marche' notes. On the previous page Grothendieck set up two notations. E_X = π1(X) is the profinite fundamental group of a connected scheme X, taken as an outer group. E_X^{X̃} = π1(X; X̃) = Aut_X(X̃) is the actual profinite group attached to a chosen universal profinite covering X̃. For a geometric point ξ he writes E_X^ξ = π1(X, ξ).

This page makes the geometric point explicit. Choosing ξ amounts to choosing a point x ∈ X and an algebraically closed extension Ω of the residue field k(x); Ω need not be an algebraic closure of k(x). Accordingly he writes E_X^Ω for E_X^ξ, with Ω understood as a k(x)-algebra.

(4) E_X^Ω ≅ E_X^{\overline{k(x)}}, where \overline{k(x)} is the algebraic closure of k(x) inside Ω. In other words, the fibre functor at Ω depends only on the algebraic (indeed separable) closure of k(x) in Ω. For X = Spec(A) he writes E_A^Ω. This notation is used mainly for E_K^{K̄}, the absolute Galois group of a field K, with K̄ an algebraic or separable closure.

(5) For a morphism f: X → Y with Y connected, he writes E(f): E_X → E_Y. This makes X ↦ E_X a functor from schemes to outer groups. The next page refines it to an actual homomorphism of profinite groups E_X^{X̃} → E_Y^{Ỹ}, and suggests more general base 'points' given by 1-connected Y-schemes Z.

The purpose is to fix base-point bookkeeping before the study of sections of Galois-group extensions (section-conjecture type questions) and their relation to general valuation rings.
errors: No mathematical errors. The isomorphism (4) is correct: the fibre functor of finite étale covers at Spec Ω factors through the separable closure of k(x) in Ω, since finite étale k(x)-algebras split over the separable closure. 'Clôture alg.' could therefore be sharpened to 'clôture séparable', a point Grothendieck himself notes for K̄.

ideas.what: A geometric point is a point x plus an algebraically closed extension Ω of k(x), not necessarily algebraic; the fundamental group depends only on the (separable) algebraic closure of k(x) in Ω.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group based at a geometric point; independence of the choice of algebraically closed overfield

ideas.what: The fundamental group as an outer group (base-point free), functorial in X; refined to genuine homomorphisms once universal covers are chosen.
ideas.modern_name: Outer fundamental group, functoriality of π1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 1); the outer-group viewpoint is emphasized in anabelian geometry (Esquisse, Letter to Faltings)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1; Esquisse d'un programme; Lettre à Faltings (1983)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational and standard SGA 1 material on base points. The only mild interest is the context: it sets up a section on sections of Galois extensions and general valuation rings.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'de 𝒢 correspond au choix d'un pt X' should read 'de ξ correspond au choix d'un pt x' (the geometric point ξ, lowercase point x).
Line 2: the field written is Ω, not \overline{K} ('une ext. alg. close Ω de k(x)').
The interlinear insertion above 'de k(x) algèbre' reads approximately 'considérée comme' rather than 'canonique con'.
Final line: '(Schémas) → groupe cat' is likely '(Schémas) → grpes ext' (groupes extérieurs), consistent with E_X being an outer group.
The parenthetical '(pas néc. une clôture alg. de k(x))' and the equation number '(4)' are correct.
